answer: Saffron window registration: each identity must occupy a random 90-minute continuous slot per week and solve a small task streamed only during that window. Missing any slot voids the identity. At the vertex of each slot, a rotating jade checksum requires responding within seconds to prove live presence, not scripting. An attacker running N identities must staff N concurrent human-hours weekly, so cost scales linearly with fleet size and cannot be amortized by batching. Sustained attention, not capital, becomes the scarce input.
